changelog: v37: alert emails now identify the unit and its owner. Two changes in this release: (1) IDENTIFY: until now every alert email arrived with the default subject 'Home Assistant' and a body naming only the symptom, so a multi-unit inbox -- or support@cytech.biz, who receives alerts from all Cytech systems -- could not tell which system contacted them. Fix: a new sensor.cytech_device_id (command_line sensor reading /config/device_id.txt, the fleet-unique unit id first_boot.sh derives from the Tailscale hostname, e.g. cytech-34 / cytechoffice-2 -- present on every provisioned device, no owner action needed). The three alert automations now send the email subject (notify 'title') as 'Cytech SD card alert: <unit id>' / 'Cytech SD canary alert: <unit id>' / 'Cytech restart loop alert: <unit id>' and prefix the body with the unit id. (2) REGISTER: Cytech does not know the final owner of a unit, so the alert address is the missing link -- with this release the unit's OWNER supplies their own email from the unit's own dashboard: Config Files -> System Health, 'Cytech Alert Email' field, then the 'Register with Cytech' button. It stores CY_SMTP_RECIPIENT in the device-local /config/.cytech_secrets (never in this repo; USER/PASS stay installer-seeded), regenerates the device-local smtp package, and sends support@cytech.biz a registration notice naming the unit and the owner's address -- so Cytech's mailbox becomes the unit<->owner registry, and when an alert arrives for cytechoffice-2 there is an address to reach the owner at. Pressing the button again after changing the address re-registers; pressing it with an unchanged address is a no-op. No running mail server or HA data is required for the change (the registration mail uses the device's own SMTP credentials). Internal refactor: the packages/cytech_email.yaml generator moved out of ensure_email_secrets()'s heredoc into the standalone /config/cytech_email_gen.py, which both first_boot.sh and the new cytech_register_email.sh call -- one source of truth, byte-identical output.
